title: What is known about 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_0LB1LF_1RE1LC_1LC0RB_0LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_0LB1LF_1RE1LC_1LC0RB_0LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At the visits of the head (state B) to the left end the tape is B>0 0 [10] 1^N S. The measured map is N → (3N + c)/2, c depending on N mod 4 and on the prefix, and the right word S grows when N is odd. Lean proves the fourteen shift rules of the sweeps; the map is measured by simulation, not proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 44,593 cells have been visited and 33,805 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Fourteen rules over 3-cell words, each for every n and every tape around; e.g. E turns (110)<sup>n</sup> into (001)<sup>n</sup> going right, C turns (110)<sup>n</sup> into (101)<sup>n</sup> going left.

claims.title: The measured map
claims.text: From K(pre, N, S) = B>0 0 pre 1^N S, with pre empty and S empty: N = 4j → (empty, 3N/2 + 4, empty); N = 4j + 2 → (10, 3N/2 + 2, empty); N = 4j + 1 → (10, (3N + 1)/2, 011); N = 4j + 3 → (empty, (3N + 5)/2, 011). With pre = 10 the offsets are 7, 5, 7/2, 11/2. Measured for N = 20..31.

claims.title: The run
claims.text: Samples of the run from blank tape have N = 175, 263, 395, 584, 923, 1388, 2090, 3140, 4717, 7074, 10624, 15940, 23914, 35873, 53811 (to 1.7·109 steps): ratio 3/2. Between samples, each round trip turns 4 ones into two words 110 (at 109 steps B>0 0 a^8705 1^18465, a = 110).

claims.title: Rounds between end events, by remainder class
claims.text: Sample the run whenever the head is in state B reading 1 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A U^m B: one long periodic block between two short context words. For each class (A, U, B, m mod 4) the next sample is simulated for six values of m and extended as an affine map of m (with a cubic step count). Along the direct run from blank tape to 3·109 steps (26 events) the class map predicts the next event in all 15 rounds it applies to. This is an extrapolation checked by computation, not a proof.

claims.title: 448 rounds of the class map without a halt
claims.text: Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 41,888 of the run (A = 11, U = 100, m = 87, B = 1): 448 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 178 bits (about 10108 steps of the machine). 38 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 6,267 cells. The iteration stops there, at a context too large for the six simulations (a second long block has formed); this is a limit of the tool, not an event of the machine.

claims.title: No halting class among 22 contexts
claims.text: Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 22 contexts expanded, 22 found, to depth 9. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 8 contexts longer than 300 cells were not expanded.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Open: the map's effect on the right word S (a counter) is not worked out, and the halting transition (F reading 1) is not located.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LC_1LC0RF_0LF1LD_0LE---_1RF1LC_1LE0RA up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LC_1LA1RE_1LD1RE_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. A block of ones is converted, four cells at a time, into a run of the word 110 and rebuilt half as long again: a Collatz-like map n → about 3n/2, with a one-bit prefix and a small counter on the right that listen to the remainders.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The measured map, c from N mod 4 and the prefix.

sections.heading: Does any remainder class halt?
html: A generic test used on the whole family: sample the run whenever the head is in state B reading 1 with only 0s to its right. Read leftwards from the head, the tape is then A Um B, one long periodic block between two short context words A and B. The round to the next sample is computed class by class: for a class (A, U, B, m mod 4) six values of m are simulated, and when they agree the round is taken to be an affine map of m. Against the direct run to 3·109 steps the class map is right in all 15 rounds it applies to. It is an observed law, not a proved one.

The orbit. Iterated with exact integers from the event at step 41,888 of the run (A = 11, U = 100, m = 87, B = 1): 448 rounds without meeting a halting class; m then has 178 bits (about 10108 steps of the machine). 38 distinct contexts occur, the longest of 6,267 cells. The iteration stops there, at a context too large for the six simulations (a second long block has formed); this is a limit of the tool, not an event of the machine.

Can any class halt? Breadth first from the starting context, with every remainder at every context (whether or not the numbers can really produce that sequence of remainders, and only for m large compared with the contexts): 22 contexts expanded, 22 found, to depth 9. None of them halts; the search is not complete (the set of contexts keeps growing), and it says nothing about a halt that needs a context as long as the block itself. 8 contexts longer than 300 cells were not expanded.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.493). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.045).
After 109 steps the tape spans 44,593 cells (31,896 left of the start, 58 right), with a density of 1s of 0.758.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Ones turning into 110s
html: At step 999,378,935 the left side is B>0 0 a^8705 1^18465 with a = 110; one round trip later it is a^8707 1^18461: four ones became two words 110, two cells more. When the ones are used up the run of 110 is rebuilt into a block of ones, and the sample is B>0 0 [10] 1^N S again, with N about 3/2 larger (175, 263, 395, 584, 923, 1388, 2090, …, 35873, 53811).

sections.heading: N → (3N + c)/2
html:
prefix empty, S empty:
  N = 4j   → 3N/2 + 4,    prefix empty
  N = 4j+2 → 3N/2 + 2,    prefix 10
  N = 4j+1 → (3N+1)/2,    prefix 10,    S = 011
  N = 4j+3 → (3N+5)/2,    prefix empty, S = 011

Worked example: K(∅, 24, ∅) → K(∅, 40, ∅) → K(∅, 64, ∅) → K(∅, 100, ∅) → K(∅, 154, ∅). Odd N lengthen the word S at the right end, which acts as a slow counter; its later shapes (e.g. 0110111111011) change the offsets. Measured, not proved.

sections.heading: Open
html: The halting transition is F reading 1. The 3n/2 map itself never stops; whether the machine halts depends on what the right-end counter S does when it is fed by the odd values of N, which has not been worked out. Its sister machine 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_1LB1LF_1LE1RE_0LA0RB_0LB---, which shares rows A, B and D, runs a 4n/3 map instead.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1LC_1LC0RF_0LF1LD_0LE---_1RF1LC_1LE0RA: rename A→E, B→F, C→C, D→A, E→B, F→D; it is this table started in state D
  • 1RB0LC_1LA1RE_1LD1RE_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RB---: rename A→B, B→A, C→E, D→C, E→D, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror

summary: A block of N ones at the left is turned, 4 ones into two words 110 per round trip, and rebuilt about 3/2 as long: a Collatz-like map N → (3N + c)/2 with c set by N mod 4, a one-bit prefix and a word growing at the right end; halting not reduced yet.
